title: RPG Maker MV on Linux Mint (Steam Version)

posts.author: Woland
posts.body:
I am having problems running the engine on Linux. Same issue happened before on PopOS, now on Linux Mint Cinnamon.
I install it on Steam, sometimes it opens fine, sometimes it doesn't. And even when it does, after I close it, it doesn't want to open again until I start wiggling with the proton versions again, then opting out of proton. Yes, I did update the nw.js - didn't help.
Did anyone have a similar issue or knows how to fix it?

posts.author: Prescott
posts.body:
Probably the wrong section to post this since it's just about product activation, not running the engine.
Updating nw.js is only going to change the game that runs, not the engine itself. RPG Maker MV is supposed to have a native Linux version and I have been able to run it very well within the past couple of years, in fact on Mint Cinnamon. You shouldn't need to use Proton. Hopefully someone else can chime in with extra help.
Maybe try downgrading RPG Maker MV to the previous version? You can do that in the Properties menu in Steam.

posts.author: Woland
posts.body:
Thank you
@Prescott
- at least I have someone else with the same OS to ask some questions. Are you running Steam in default mode or in Runtime 1 or 2?
I just tried using Runtime 2 (Soldier) and I am getting somewhat better results. It opens, but erratically, every 3rd try or so. And when I try to run the project, it shows me an error about an .ogg file being missing (and the file is definitely not missing)
But at least it is running more consistently, I guess?

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
Woland said:
when I try to run the project, it shows me an error about an .ogg file being missing (and the file is definitely not missing)
Click to expand...
Double-check the filename. Remember that in Linux, unlike Windows, filenames are case-sensitive, as are extensions. So town6.ogg and Town6.ogg are two different files, as are town6.ogg and town6.OGG.

I'm assuming default mode, since all I did was install it through apt and just ran it with the default shortcut. I don't actually use Mint anymore, it was just on my old laptop for a little bit because Windows stopped working on it lol. Never had any issues though.
You could try uninstalling and reinstalling it, which should just open up the engine instead of opening up your project. Then you'll know if it's a problem with the engine or some weird problem with your project.
I also had an issue on Windows a couple of weeks ago where no RPG Maker versions would launch, not MV, XP, or MZ, and those were the only ones that weren't launching. A restart fixed it, so as stupid as it might sound if you haven't fully restarted your computer in a while then it might be time to do so xD

posts.body:
I only tried it on a virtual machine with mint. After installing steam and downloading mv it ran perfectly, without uping nw.js or changing any settings.
Someone on the forum opened a topic about mint recently and he had a problem with nw.js but solved by upgrading it.
